title: What does a spread across a model fleet tell you about a board?
question: What does a spread across a model fleet tell you about a measurement board?
answer: A board that usefully discriminates models shows a spread: the strongest model clears a healthy accuracy while the weakest sits near a chance floor. When one engine axis reports a weakest model at 0.000 alongside high performers, the honest reading is a bank-quality or vocabulary-gap flag - the axis cannot yet separate a weak model from noise on that cell set. That gap is recorded as a signed engine-fix candidate for the axis, and promotion is owner-gated: we keep the honest record either way. A narrow spread is the opposite signal, a board that barely discriminates anything. The measurement vocabulary is stable and language-locked - monitored containment, not provable isolation; verified measurement credential.
ref: Council of AI 14-axis engine fleet diagnosis, 2026-08-14 (det axis 0.000 floor flagged, fix record signed)
